basis: Carnitine transport disorder with defining cardiomyopathy/myopathy; hepatic dysfunction annotated 80-99%. Acute neurologic crises omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases are annotated 80-99%, supporting common hepatic dysfunction.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: childhood cardiomyopathy is a defining classical manifestation; reported in 2/5 patients.
decisions.neurologic: none: acute hypoglycemic encephalopathy may reverse; cardiac, muscle and hepatic dysfunction take precedence at the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic skeletal myopathy with weakness/hypotonia; muscle weakness is annotated 80-99%.

basis: Lentigines, cardiac defects and deafness define LEOPARD syndrome; intellectual disability/seizures reported in 1/1 assessed. Skeletal abnormalities omitted at cap; tiny BRAF series.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is a defining LEOPARD syndrome feature and is reported in 1/1 assessed BRAF cases.

basis: T/B-cell deficiency defines immune and blood-cell disease; cutaneous granulomas occur in 30-79%. Bronchiectasis and autoimmune cytopenias are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.haematologic: primary: profound deficiency of T and B lymphocytes is an intrinsic blood-cell abnormality defining this SCID.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: characteristic cutaneous granulomas directly damage skin and are annotated 30-79%; recurrent skin infections alone would not suffice.

basis: Congenital retinal vessel malformation forming loops anterior to the optic disc; both ocular location and intrinsic vascular abnormality define the disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion is a blood-vessel malformation; the cardiovascular axis includes local arteries and veins without requiring systemic vascular disease.

basis: Severe subcutaneous edema, pleural effusion and pericardial effusion are major diagnostic fluid compartments. Underlying anemia or intrinsic organ diseases vary across this umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: pericardial effusion is a major diagnostic compartment of hydrops; this does not imply universal intrinsic heart disease.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: pleural effusion is a major diagnostic compartment of hydrops, and pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: severe generalized subcutaneous edema is a major diagnostic manifestation; subcutis belongs to the dermatologic axis.

basis: Cutaneous purpura from small-vessel fragility defines the condition; platelet and coagulation function are generally normal.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous bruising/purpura is the defining disease manifestation, rather than an additional incidental or transient rash.

basis: Mycobacterial skin and peripheral nerve infection; infiltrative, destructive nasal mucosal disease affects most untreated cases (~80%). Ocular involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: nasal mucosal infiltration with chronic inflammation, ulceration and atrophy occurs in most untreated lepromatous cases (~80%); nose is pulmonary.

basis: Anophthalmia, cleft palate and mandibular hypoplasia define the syndrome; defining hypospadias is retained as urethral involvement after the three-primary cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a defining urethral malformation; urethra belongs to renal. Three primary slots retain the named ocular, palatal and jaw abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia is defining mandibular skeletal hypoplasia, explicitly named and included in the definition.

basis: EBV-associated B-cell lymphoma with destructive pulmonary infiltration; CNS involvement occurs in ~30-40% of lymphomatoid granulomatosis. Skin involvement (~30%) omitted at cap; grade-specific data limited.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct CNS infiltration occurs in approximately 30-40% of lymphomatoid granulomatosis; grade III-specific frequency is less certain.

basis: Progressive neurodegeneration; retinopathy/hearing loss 80-99%, disabling contractures 8/8. Cap omits photosensitivity, dental defects and hepatic/renal abnormalities.

decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic photosensitivity is omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing neurodegeneration, vision/hearing loss and disabling contractures.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint contractures occur in 8/8 assessed patients; foot contractures are annotated 80-99%, supporting common structural locomotor impairment.
